messages:
alice-support: Customer on Dedicated reporting intermittent 429s during a midday traffic spike. They insist they're under the project quota and only a single API key in use. Sample log: `429 quota_exceeded scope=org`.

derek-cs: customer says requests come from an AWS NAT gateway; they rotate ephemeral IPs. All requests are authenticated with the same API key in the `Authorization` header.

ben-sre: quick check — our quota attribution can pick org, project, api_key, or ip depending on detect order. If NAT collapse is on, IP-based bursts may attribute to org in some heuristics. Can you paste the raw request headers and 1-2 request ids?

alice-support: pasted two request ids: `req_01H9XH8A1Y`, `req_01H9XH8A2Z`. Headers (redacted):
```
Authorization: Bearer sk-live-XYZ
X-Forwarded-For: 10.0.0.22
CF-Connecting-IP: 3.122.45.11
User-Agent: Redwood-Client/1.8
```
Note: customer is behind Cloud NAT -> provider NAT mapping; source IP seen by us is `3.122.45.11`.

carla-engr: that CF header plus XFF could confuse our scope detection. The quota service prefers API key then project then org, but there was a recent fallback change that prefers IP when the key is missing or flagged. Maybe the key was momentarily rejected and we landed on IP scoping.

nina-devex: customer also said they see a 401-misrouted earlier in the day for a different key; maybe transient auth hiccup caused the engine to mark requests as unauthenticated and apply IP-based limits for a few seconds.

ben-sre: checking quota logs for those req ids... (few seconds) — I see `auth: success` for both, but there's a burst subroutine that groups by IP when auth throughput crosses a threshold. For `req_01H9XH8A1Y` we logged `throttle_reason=ip_burst scope=org`.

alice-support: customer insists project-level quota is not exceeded (they sent usage snapshot). They want understanding why org-level scoping applied.

ben-sre: two possibilities: 1) a background reconciliation window collapsed per-project counters into org-level aggregates during a heavy rollup, and the burst heuristic then favored org scope to ensure global fairness; 2) a transient auth cache miss made the key appear unresolvable for ~200ms causing IP fallback.

carla-engr: adding detail — there was a deploy yesterday that adjusted the `quota_fallback_threshold` from 100r/s to 80r/s for IP aggregation. That change reduced tail latency but tightened when we switch to org/IP scopes under pressure. PR #4312.

quota-bot: [quota-service] alert muted: high ip_aggregation_events for org-id `org_9876` between 2026-02-14T15:02:00Z and 2026-02-14T15:07:00Z.

ben-sre: proposed repro for eng team and customer: run a short script that simulates 120r/s from multiple ephemeral NATed connections using same API key and ensure one run toggles auth cache TTL artificially. Here's a curl example to reproduce header shapes:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-XYZ" -H "CF-Connecting-IP: 3.122.45.11" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
If you can flip the auth cache TTL locally (simulate small auth service delay), you can force key-unresolved path.

alice-support: shared repro steps with customer and they're willing to run. They asked whether we can temporarily disable IP-aggregation for their org while they validate.

carla-engr: we can add an org-level override to prefer api_key/project scoping for 1 hour. Need a small change in the quota service config and a consent from security. I'll draft the config change and run it behind a feature flag.

ben-sre: I'll open an SRE incident and attach the quota logs + the two req ids. We should also correlate time with the dedicated pool autoscaler; if capacity dropped and we moved requests across pods, some requests may hit new auth caches.

derek-cs: customer also flagged billing — they saw unexpected token billing for failed/429 requests. Are we charging for throttled requests?

carla-engr: current billing policy charges per accepted token only; 429s shouldn't bill for new tokens. But if the request completed partial tokens before being canceled, it may count. We'll need finance to confirm any edge-case meter counts during retries.

nina-devex: added a short note for docs: include a section on NAT + NAT-gateway patterns and recommended headers (prefer `X-Real-IP` from edge) to improve scope attribution.

alice-support: customer ran the repro and saw 429s when auth cache was slowed. They accepted the temporary override. Thanks team. Next steps:
- ben-sre to file incident with logs (INC-2026-0221).
- carla-engr to push temporary org override behind flag and monitor for 1 hour.
- nina-devex to update docs and a quick troubleshooting checklist for support.
- alice-support to confirm with customer after override.

ben-sre: incident filed INC-2026-0221, assigned to eng-sre. I'll post follow-ups in the incident thread.

alice-support: marking resolved for ticket to customer pending post-override verification. :thumbsup:
